Proposition
[Strong maximum principle for systems, II] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0213 1. ch12:12.49\group Strong System Maximum Principles

If $u\geq 0$ and $\phi _k(x_0,0)>0$ for some $k$ and $x_0$, then $\phi _k(x,t)>0$ for every $x$ and every $t>0$.

Proof

\sketch ↗ thm:manifold-parabolic-strong-maximum-principle Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0213, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0214 On a relatively compact connecting domain, choose $0\leq \varphi _k\leq \phi _k(\cdot ,0)/k$, positive at $x_0$, and solve the same scalar Dirichlet problem for $f$. Put $\bar u=u+(\varepsilon e^{At}-f)\widetilde h$. If the sum $\bar\phi _k$ of its $k$ smallest eigenvalues first vanished, parallel extend an orthonormal minimizing $k$-frame. The derivative test, the null-eigenvector condition, and local Lipschitz continuity yield

\[ 0\geq (A-K)k(\varepsilon e^{At}+f), \]

contradicting $A>K$. Thus $\bar\phi _k>0$; after $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$, $\phi _k\geq kf>0$ at the arbitrary endpoint.

□
